rounds.text: Disha Resources Ltd is trading below its underlying asset backing at a price-to-book ratio of 0.89x against a book value of ₹ 38.8 [E1], representing an attractive entry point for value-focused participants. Operational momentum is rapidly improving, highlighted by a massive 457% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E16] and a 97% compounded profit growth over the same period [E17]. Furthermore, the company's working capital requirements have dramatically compressed from 5,054 days down to 25.4 days [E44], freeing up vital capital and demonstrating significantly enhanced operational efficiency. This efficiency is directly manifesting in positive financial health, with the business generating Rs 0.50 Cr in both operating cash flow and free cash flow for Mar 2026 [E31, E32] while remaining almost entirely debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E33]. Market sentiment has been slow to catch up to these fundamental improvements, creating a disconnect where results score 100/100 while the price and verdict remain cautious [E56]. Conceded: promoter holding has dropped substantially to 9.41% as of Sep 2026 from 48.10% in Dec 2023 [E36].

The most alarming risk facing Disha Resources Ltd is the precipitous collapse in promoter confidence, evidenced by promoters slashing their stake from 48.10% in December 2023 down to just 9.41% by September 2026, representing a massive 38.69 percentage point reduction [E36]. This low promoter holding of 9.41% creates an acute governance and alignment risk for outside shareholders [E48]. Compounding this ownership drain is a severe historical growth deficit, highlighted by compounded sales contractions of -17% over 5 years and -27% over 3 years [E14, E15]. Furthermore, the business fails to generate meaningful shareholder returns, sputtering along with a median return on equity of 0% across 10, 5, 3, and 1-year lookbacks [E22, E23, E24, E25], accompanied by a negative TTM ROE of -0.12% [E8] and a low interest coverage ratio [E45]. Conceded: the company boasts a positive TTM operating cash flow of Rs 0.50 Cr and has driven working capital requirements down to 25.4 days [E31, E44]. However, these operational flickers cannot mask a multi-year trajectory of contracting top-line sales [E14, E15] and an exodus of core insiders [E36].

Conceded: promoter holding has dropped significantly to 9.41% [E36]. However, the bear's focus on historical sales contractions of -17% over 5 years [E14] ignores the explosive recent reality of a 457% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E16]. The narrative of a stagnant business is further dismantled by a 97% compounded profit growth over the TTM [E17] and net profit surging by 200% year-on-year [E53]. Furthermore, the business is completely debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E33], and its operational efficiency has dramatically improved as working capital requirements plummeted from 5,054 days to just 25.4 days [E44]. Conceded: the multi-year ROE has lingered near 0% [E22, E23], but the insider-bias checklist explicitly warns against dismissing a fundamental turnaround on stale sentiment when current results score a maximum 100/100 [E56]. Operating margins are actively recovering—up 12 percentage points in the TTM and 7 percentage points in the latest quarter [E26, E27]—while generating a tangible positive free cash flow of Rs 0.50 Cr [E32].

Conceded: the company generated a positive free cash flow of Rs 0.50 Cr in Mar 2026 [E32] and improved its operating margins [E26, E27]. However, the bull's reliance on TTM sales growth of 457% [E16] ignores the structural multi-year decay shown by a 5-year compounded sales contraction of -17% [E14] and a 3-year contraction of -27% [E15]. While the business is debt-free [E33], this does not compensate for a multi-year history of zero return on equity, with a 10-year, 5-year, and 3-year median ROE of strictly 0% [E22, E23, E24]. Conceded: the rules-based screen notes net profit surging year-on-year [E53], but the fundamental earning power remains non-existent, evidenced by an annualized ROE of -0.1% [E12] and an ROCE of -0.1% [E11], falling severely short of sector benchmarks [E8, E9]. Furthermore, the bull downplays the catastrophic collapse in promoter commitment, where insider ownership cratered from 48.10% in Dec 2023 to just 9.41% in Sep 2026 [E36], leaving minority shareholders heavily exposed.
